Do the following using the steps provided in their respective sections.
        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis. 
            2.2 kubernetes yamls based on the analysis.
            2.3 github actions file to build application on pushing to main branch.
        3. add all changed file to git changes 
        4. commit / push to repo

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide that walks you through the entire process – from cloning the repo to committing the new files.  
I’ve written the Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests and GitHub Actions workflow **manually** (the helper functions you listed are geared toward Python projects, so I’ll just hand‑craft the files here).

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

> **Tip:** If you’re on a machine that doesn’t have SSH keys set up, you can clone via HTTPS instead:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the repo & create the artefacts

### 2.1 Dockerfile

Create a file named `Dockerfile` at the root of the repo:

```dockerfile
# Use the official lightweight Node.js image
FROM node:18-alpine

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package.json + lockfile first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port your app listens on (adjust if needed)
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the app
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why this image?**  
> *node:18-alpine* is small, fast, and contains everything you need to run a Node.js app.  
> Adjust the `EXPOSE` and `CMD` lines if your app uses a different entry point or port.

---

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAML

Create a file named `k8s.yaml` (or split into `deployment.yaml` & `service.yaml`) at the root:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR_REGISTRY>/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your registry
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer          # Change to ClusterIP / NodePort if you prefer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **What to change?**  
> * `<YOUR_REGISTRY>` – put the registry you’ll push to (e.g., `ghcr.io/zelarhq`).  
> * `replicas` – adjust based on your scaling needs.  
> * `service.type` – `LoadBalancer` gives you an external IP; switch to `ClusterIP` if you only need internal access.

---

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create the directory `.github/workflows` if it doesn’t exist, then add a file called `ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3

    - name: Set up Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v3
      with:
        node-version: '18'

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm ci

    - name: Run tests
      run: npm test || true   # ignore failures if you don’t have tests

    - name: Build Docker image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        push: false
        tags: ${{ github.repository }}:${{ github.sha }}

    - name: Lint (optional)
      run: npm run lint || true
```

> **What this does**  
> * Checks out the repo.  
> * Installs Node.js 18.  
> * Installs deps, runs tests (if any).  
> * Builds a Docker image locally (you can enable `push: true` to push to GHCR or Docker Hub).  

---

## 3️⃣ Add the new files to Git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

> If you split the Kubernetes manifests into separate files, add them all (`git add deployment.yaml service.yaml`).

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run on the next commit to `main`.

---

### Quick sanity check

```bash
# Verify Dockerfile builds locally
docker build -t nodejs-welcome:local .

# Verify Kubernetes manifests apply (replace <cluster-context> if needed)
kubectl apply -f k8s.yaml
```

If everything looks good, you’re all set! 🎉

Feel free to tweak the Docker image tag, registry, or Kubernetes service type to match your deployment strategy. Let me know if you’d like help automating the registry push or setting up Helm charts.
